submission.justification: Radiator-R1 at 3.3 cm thickness provides the best pion/kaon separation performance at 10 GeV/c, achieving 4.763 sigma separation based on simulation results. This represents a significant improvement over Radiator-R3 (3.881 sigma at optimal 3.5 cm) and Radiator-R2 (2.933 sigma at optimal 3-4 cm). The simulation shows that R1's performance peaks around 3.3-3.35 cm thickness, with performance degrading at both lower and higher thicknesses. All three radiators are presented as viable candidates in the project documentation, and the vessel will be flushed with dry nitrogen during operation to help preserve radiator properties. Given that the primary goal is to achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation, and R1 provides ~23% better separation than R3 and ~65% better than R2, this represents the optimal choice for the detector's physics performance.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as 'high-index porous radiator' and is one of the three candidates.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: No explicit ageing test data is provided in any of the project documents for any of the three radiator candidates. However, all three radiators are presented as viable candidates, which implies they meet minimum operational requirements. The vessel will be flushed with dry nitrogen during operation (per gas_volume.md), which helps mitigate humidity-related degradation. Radiator-R3 has hydrophobic treatment specifically for ageing resistance, but absence of ageing test data prevents definitive verification of R1's compliance with the <10% transparency loss requirement.
Recommended thickness of 3.3 cm is within the specified range of 1-6 cm.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 at 3.3 cm achieves 4.763 sigma separation, which is the highest performance among all tested configurations. This exceeds R3's best performance (3.881 sigma at 3.5 cm) by 23% and R2's best performance (2.933 sigma at 3-4 cm) by 62%.
